{{Short description|List of the finals of the FLLA World Cup}}

[[File:Map_of_FLLA_World_Cup_finals_winners.png|thumb|upright=1.8|Nations that have reached an FLLA World Cup final, shaded by the number of finals won]]

The '''[[FLLA World Cup]]''' is an international [[Arraby]] competition contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]], the sport's global governing body. The competition has been held every four years since the inaugural tournament in 1656, staged at the time as the Ayuman Continental Tournament, with the exception of four editions cancelled because of intercontinental conflict. The '''final''' is the last match of the competition, played by the two teams that have come through the [[FLLA World Cup#Final tournament|knockout stage]], and the winners are crowned world champions.<ref name="fllaheritage">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/roll-of-honour|title=FLLA World Cup roll of honour|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=20 August 1764}}</ref>

Twenty-four finals have been contested between the [[1656 FLLA World Cup|1656 edition]] and the [[1764 FLLA World Cup|1764 edition]]. Twelve different national teams have appeared as champions. [[Lycroa]] are the most successful side, having won the trophy five times and reached the final on eight occasions, both records; [[Raledria]] are second with four titles, and [[Emara]] third with three. The reigning champions are [[Easuhura]], who defeated [[Emara]] 2–1 in the [[1764 FLLA World Cup|1764 final]] at the Tirna National Stadium in [[Tirna]] to claim their first title.<ref name="flla1764final">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/competitions/world-cup/1764/final|title=1764 FLLA World Cup final: Easuhura 2–1 Emara|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=14 July 1764}}</ref>

Three finals have been settled without a decisive result in normal or extra time: the [[1680 FLLA World Cup|1680 final]], the only final in the tournament's history to be decided by the toss of a coin, and the [[1732 FLLA World Cup|1732]], [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744]] and [[1752 FLLA World Cup|1752]] finals, each settled by a [[wikipedia:Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. The largest winning margin in a final is the five goals by which [[Lycroa]] defeated [[Emara]] 6–1 at the [[1660 FLLA World Cup|1660 final]], a record that still stands.<ref name="fllarecords">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/records|title=FLLA World Cup final records and milestones|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=22 August 1764}}</ref>

The [[1664 FLLA World Cup|1664]], [[1688 FLLA World Cup|1688]], [[1692 FLLA World Cup|1692]] and [[1696 FLLA World Cup|1696]] editions were awarded a host but never contested, the 1664 tournament because of the [[Great Imperial War]] and the remaining three because of the [[Red War]] (1688 to 1695) and the subsequent reconstruction. No final was played at these editions, and they are excluded from the table above.

==Results by confederation==

Sides from the [[AYFVL]], the Ayuman confederation, have won sixteen of the twenty-four finals and have appeared in the final on twenty occasions, fourteen of them in all-Ayuman finals. The [[ATFVL]] (Atirhan) confederation has provided six champions and the [[NAFVL]] ([[New Ayre]]) and [[QUFVL]] ([[Quia]]) confederations one each; the [[MAFVL]] ([[Mahea]]) and [[MSFVL]] ([[Massir]]) have each reached the final once without winning, while the [[ACFVL]] has yet to provide a finalist.<ref name="fllaheritage" />

Of the twenty-four finals, fourteen were contested between two [[AYFVL]] sides. Four finals have not featured an Ayuman side: the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700]] and [[1708 FLLA World Cup|1708]] finals, both between [[ATFVL]] and [[NAFVL]] sides; the [[1748 FLLA World Cup|1748 final]] between [[New Misos]] ([[ATFVL]]) and [[Seytinemas]] ([[MAFVL]]); and the [[1756 FLLA World Cup|1756 final]], in which [[Quidic]] of the [[QUFVL]] defeated [[New Misos]] of the [[ATFVL]].

==Notes==

* The [[1680 FLLA World Cup|1680 final]] between [[Lycroa]] and [[Eldjo]] finished goalless after extra time and, with the penalty shoot-out not yet in use, was decided by the toss of a coin, which Lycroa won. It is the only final in the competition's history to be settled in this way.
* Penalty shoot-outs decided the [[1732 FLLA World Cup|1732]] (Lycroa beat Emara after a 2–2 draw), [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744]] (Lycroa beat Easuhura 3–0 on penalties after a 0–0 draw) and [[1752 FLLA World Cup|1752]] finals (Praesyu beat Verusa 5–4 on penalties after a 1–1 draw).
* The first seven finals, from [[1656 FLLA World Cup|1656]] to [[1684 FLLA World Cup|1684]], were contested while the competition was staged as the Ayuman Continental Tournament; the tournament was rebranded the FLLA World Cup for the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]].
